abandon:
usage: atelier abandon ID [--note TEXT] [--delivered-by tN]
Closes the task without merging it. The holder's write token is revoked; the history and evidence stay. `--note` says why. `--delivered-by` records that the merged task tN delivered it, for work another task already brought in.
Flags:
  --note TEXT        why; kept with the event
  --delivered-by tN  a merged task that delivered this one's work; kept with the event
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier abandon t3 --note "Superseded by t5" --project demo
accept:
usage: atelier accept ID [--head SHA] [--override-review REASON [--quote WORDS]] [--note TEXT]
The developer accepts the task at its current head; `--head` names that head, and any other is refused. `--note` keeps the developer's word on the acceptance with it in the ledger. It is refused unless the gate is clear. When the change still lacks its independent review because no reviewer qualifies, `--override-review` overrides that review and accepts: the reason is required, the override is recorded as an event of its own, never as a review, and the task page and the inbox show it with its reason. The developer's direction confirms it: `--quote` with the developer's own words and `--as H/M` (or ATELIER_ACTOR) naming the model acting on them, both recorded with the override and shown on the task page, in the status and in the receipt. Without them the developer token alone does not override, nor does the browser session it signs in: the developer first presses Allow an override from the command line on the task's page, confirming with a factor no agent holds, the Cloudflare Access sign-in where the pages are behind Access, else the server's confirmation secret (OVERRIDE_SECRET), which allows one override of that revision for 15 minutes; without either the command is refused, naming the page and the factor. A project set up with `atelier init --no-override` refuses every override.
Flags:
  --head SHA                the revision accepted; the task's current head unless given, and any other is refused
  --override-review REASON  accepts without the independent review, when no reviewer qualifies; the reason is recorded, and it is confirmed by the developer's direction (--quote) or allowed first on the task's page with the Access sign-in or the server's confirmation secret
  --quote WORDS             with --override-review, the developer's own words directing the override; with --as H/M, the model acting on them, they confirm it with the developer token alone, and both are recorded with it
  --note TEXT               the developer's word on the acceptance, kept with it in the ledger
  --as H/M                  with --override-review, the harness/model overriding for the developer, kept beside them as its acting model; required with --quote
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier accept t3 --project demo
approvals:
usage: atelier approvals [--all]
       atelier approvals withdraw ID [--note T]
Lists the approvals that stand, each with its kind, revision and expiry. `--all` adds the used, withdrawn and expired ones.
The developer withdraws an approval no ship has used, so none can use it.
Flags:
  --all        adds the used, withdrawn and expired approvals
  --note TEXT  with withdraw, why; kept with the event
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier approvals --all --project demo
approve:
usage: atelier approve ACTION --head SHA [--note T] [--expires 24h]
The developer approves one protected action, such as `deploy`, `install`, `paid-run` or `photos-writeback`, at one exact revision of the main line: the full SHA of a commit the baseline holds. `atelier ship` uses the approval once, at that revision only, and a later revision needs its own. It stands for 24 hours unless `--expires` gives from `1m` to `30d`; `--note` records why. Any other kind must be one the project's ship files name.
Flags:
  --head SHA          the full revision of the main line the approval is for; required
  --note TEXT         why; kept with the approval
  --expires DURATION  how long it stands, from 1m to 30d; 24h unless given
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier approve deploy --head 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567 --project demo
base-token:
usage: atelier base-token ID
Reads a token for the repository the task is measured against: the plan's fork for a part, the baseline otherwise.
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier base-token t3 --project demo
baseline-token:
usage: atelier baseline-token
Reads a token for the project's baseline, main as it is now, with the project's regenerate command: a build's runner merges that main into the workspace before it submits (t435). A runner token may read it for any project it serves, where base-token answers only for the job the runner holds.
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier baseline-token --project demo --as claude-code/opus
block:
usage: atelier block [ID] "what it is waiting on" [--until YYYY-MM-DD]
The holder or the developer blocks the task with what it is waiting on. It keeps its holder and workspace, leaves the runner queue and stuck detection, cannot be pushed, submitted, reviewed, handed off or released, and sits in the developer's inbox with the reason until it is unblocked. With `--until` (a real UTC calendar date, today or later) the block records the last day the wait is expected to hold; from the day after, `atelier status` groups it on one line per project with its unblock and abandon commands instead of a row, and it stays blocked until it is unblocked or abandoned.
Flags:
  --until YYYY-MM-DD  the last UTC day the wait is expected to hold, today or later; refused if it is missing, not a real calendar date or in the past, and nothing is recorded then. From the next day status shows the block as expired, still blocked
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier block t3 "Waiting on the schema decision" --project demo
board:
usage: atelier board [--json]
Lists every task with its kind, title, ledger-derived stage and holder, and how many are merged.
Flags:
  --json  prints the ledger snapshot shared with the project page
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier board --project demo
branch:
usage: atelier branch push [NAME] [--force]
       atelier branch fetch NAME [--force]
       atelier branch ls
The developer carries work in progress to their other Macs: pushes the checkout's branch `wip/NAME` (the current branch unless NAME is given; a NAME without `wip/` is taken under it) to the project's branches repository beside the baseline, with a developer-only token minted for that repository alone, and records its last commit and this Mac. main, the project's branch, a task's id and any name outside `wip/` are refused before any token is minted, and the baseline's main is never reached: it changes only through landing and sync. `--force` replaces a branch the push would not fast-forward.
Fetches the developer's branch `wip/NAME` from the project's branches repository into the checkout's `wip/NAME`, which must not be the branch checked out. `--force` replaces a local branch the fetch would not fast-forward.
Lists the developer's branches, newest push first, each with its last commit and the Mac it was pushed from, as `atelier status --project` does.
Flags:
  --force  push or fetch a branch that does not fast-forward, replacing the other side's
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier branch push wip/idea --project demo
check:
usage: atelier check [--merged] [-- CMD]
Runs each required check, or the command after `--`, in a clean clone of exactly the head Artifacts holds, measures which paths changed since the baseline, and records each result as Observed. `--merged` runs them on the would-be merge, the head merged with main as main is now, in a temporary merge commit that is never pushed; the result is recorded against both revisions, shown beside the merge preview, and goes stale when either moves. A local check runs with the caller's file access, so it can read their files and Keychain and reach the network; it is given only the environment variables toolchains need, and Atelier's tokens are redacted from its output before upload. Atelier has no sandbox for checks, so do not check code you do not trust.
A local check runs on this machine with your file access: it can read your files and your Keychain and reach the network. It is given only PATH, HOME and the few other environment variables toolchains need, and Atelier's tokens are redacted from its output before it is uploaded. Atelier has no sandbox for checks: do not run code you do not trust.
Flags:
  --merged  runs the checks on the head merged with main as it is now, in a temporary merge commit that is never pushed; the result is recorded against both revisions
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier check --merged
check-log:
usage: atelier check-log ID [--head SHA]
Prints the retained logs of every check attempt at a head: the ledger head unless `--head` names one the task stood at earlier. Each attempt is labelled by check, its number among that check's runs at the head, its outcome (passed, failed, not applicable, or on the merge with main), where and when it ran and its evidence id, then its log: the whole log where the run stored one, else the inline tail (the last 3,500 characters of a check run on a machine, the last 4,000 of a container's), labelled as a tail; a stored log that can no longer be read is labelled unavailable and the tail stands in. A failed check run on a machine whose output outgrew its tail also kept the lines naming the failure, read from the whole output (at most 40 lines and 4,000 characters), and they are printed first. Atelier's tokens were redacted from a local check's output before it was recorded.
Flags:
  --head SHA  the revision whose attempts to print, 7 to 64 hex digits; the ledger head unless given, and a head the task stood at earlier may be named
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier check-log t3 --project demo
claim:
usage: atelier claim ID --as H/M [--runner home:NAME]
Makes the claimant the task's holder, forks the baseline into the task's workspace, mints a write token for the claimant alone, clones the workspace and records the project's branch as the one it pushes to. Claiming again refreshes the token and that branch, saying when the branch changed. `--runner` names the runner when a runner claims a dispatched task.
Flags:
  --runner home:NAME  names the runner, when a runner claims a dispatched task
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier claim t3 --project demo --as claude-code/opus-5.5
clean:
usage: atelier clean [--project NAME] [--dry-run]
Removes the workspaces of merged or abandoned tasks whose HEAD is the head Atelier recorded or in main, and stale check clones. Removal is permanent, not to the Trash. A workspace with changed files, ignored files other than rebuildable output (such as a harness's logs under .scratch/ or a .env), or commits neither Atelier nor main holds is kept, and its KEEP line says why. `--dry-run` previews.
Flags:
  --project NAME  the project whose clones are looked at; this folder's project unless given
  --dry-run       lists what would be removed and removes nothing
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier clean --project demo
clear-secret:
usage: atelier clear-secret ID --note "why"
The developer clears the task's standing secret flags with the reason the flagged lines are safe, as the web page's Clear secret flag does. The reason is kept against each line's file and fingerprint, so a later push that keeps the identical line is not flagged again. A scan still pending has no flag to clear.
Flags:
  --note TEXT  why the flagged lines are safe; required, at most 500 characters, kept with the clearance
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier clear-secret t3 --note "A fake key in a test fixture" --project demo
clone:
usage: atelier clone PROJECT [DIR] [--replace] [--private-home DIR]
Makes this Mac's checkout of a project from its baseline: clones the baseline's main, with every Git hook off, with its whole history and the receipts on `refs/notes/atelier` into DIR (`~/ai-projects/PROJECT` unless given, which must be missing or empty), keeps the baseline as origin, with no token kept in the checkout (each command that reaches the baseline mints its own, as `sync` does), sets the project's commit identity, and registers DIR as the project's checkout on this Mac. A baseline holding part of the history is registered as one, each of its commits paired with itself. A project already registered here at another path is refused unless `--replace` is given. This Mac keeps a copy of the project's list of private files (`.atelier-private` in its iCloud folder), which every push is checked against.
Flags:
  --replace           registers DIR in place of the checkout this Mac already registers for the project; that folder is left as it is
  --private-home DIR  the folder that keeps the project's private files and their list, in place of the iCloud ai-projects folder named for the project
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier clone demo ~/ai-projects/demo
criteria-finding:
usage: atelier criteria-finding ID --review N --index N --verdict confirmed|refuted|fixed [--note TEXT]
The developer answers one finding of a criteria review: refuted, that it was wrong; fixed, that it is answered; confirmed, that it stands and the criteria still need the change. Refuted and fixed settle a finding. An approval of the revision counts only once every blocking finding on it is settled, and a rejection whose blocking findings are all settled is reviewed again rather than changed. `--review` names the criteria review and `--index` the finding's position in it, one based. Build and code-review briefs carry the findings with these answers.
Flags:
  --review N   the criteria review's number, as atelier show prints it; required
  --index N    the finding's position in that review's findings, one based; required
  --verdict V  confirmed, refuted or fixed; refuted and fixed settle the finding; required
  --note TEXT  why; kept with the verdict and shown in later briefs
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier criteria-finding t3 --review 4 --index 1 --verdict refuted --note "The test named in the brief observes it" --project demo
criteria-review:
usage: atelier criteria-review ID [--reviewer H/M]
The developer asks for a review of the task's acceptance criteria before it is built, apart from any review of the change: a model of another family than every model that wrote the criteria judges whether each can be observed and whether the set says what the brief requires. The criteria are kept by revision with their authors, and the review binds to the revision they are at now; any edit of the criteria takes the approval back for good, an identical edit changes nothing, and a verdict that arrives after an edit is refused. `--reviewer` names the reviewer; otherwise the pool picks one. It is refused when no author is recorded, when a model author's family is not recognised, when no reviewer qualifies, and while a rejection's blocking findings wait for the developer. Under `init --require-criteria-review` a build is dispatched and claimed only while the approval stands; a plan asks for the review itself before it dispatches each part.
Flags:
  --reviewer H/M  names the reviewer, which must be of another family than every model that wrote the criteria; otherwise the pool picks one
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier criteria-review t3 --project demo
criteria-review-claim:
usage: atelier criteria-review-claim ID [--runner home:NAME]
A reviewer's runner claims the open review of the task's acceptance criteria and gets the brief the server built, the revision and binding of the criteria the verdict must name, and the review's number. The reviewer reads no code: the criteria are judged before the build. `--runner` names the runner.
Flags:
  --runner home:NAME  names the runner that claims the criteria review
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier criteria-review-claim t3 --runner home:studio --project demo
criteria-review-failed:
usage: atelier criteria-review-failed ID --request N [--note TEXT]
A reviewer whose harness stopped, timed out or wrote no valid verdict records the failure on the criteria review it claimed. The review approves nothing, and the criteria may be asked about again.
Flags:
  --request N  the criteria review's number, as the claim gave it; required
  --note TEXT  why no verdict was reached; kept with the review
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier criteria-review-failed t3 --request 4 --note "The harness timed out" --project demo
criteria-verdict:
usage: atelier criteria-verdict ID --approve|--reject --rev N --criteria BINDING --request N [--note TEXT] [--findings JSON] [--checks JSON]
Records a verdict on the review of the task's acceptance criteria the reviewer claimed. `--rev`, `--criteria` and `--request` name the revision, the binding and the review the claim gave; a verdict for a revision the criteria have left is refused and records nothing. `--findings` attaches the findings, each naming the criterion it concerns; a rejection needs a blocking one and an approval allows none. `--checks` flags the criteria the builder cannot verify in its workspace (a signed-in browser, production data, a human step), each the developer's or the orchestrator's check after deploy; a flagged criterion blocks nothing, the build brief says not to claim it verified, and the review of the change may defer it. An approval counts only once the developer has settled every blocking finding any review raised on that revision.
Flags:
  --approve           the criteria can be observed and say what the brief requires; allows no blocking finding
  --reject            at least one blocking finding names a criterion that cannot be judged, contradicts the brief, or leaves the task open
  --rev N             the revision of the criteria the claim gave; a verdict for any other is refused; required
  --criteria BINDING  the 64-digit binding of the criteria the claim gave; required
  --request N         the criteria review's number, as the claim gave it; required
  --note TEXT         the reviewer's summary; kept with the verdict
  --findings JSON     a JSON list of findings, each {file, line, severity, text}, the file naming the criterion as criterion-N or criteria
  --checks JSON       a JSON list of checks after deploy, each {criterion, by, text}: the criterion's number, owner or orchestrator, and what is checked once deployed
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier criteria-verdict t3 --approve --rev 1 --criteria 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef --request 4 --note "Each criterion names a test" --project demo
decide:
usage: atelier decide "text" --quote "developer's words" [--project P] [--as H/M]
The developer records a standing decision for the project, dated, with their own words it rests on: another company reviews everywhere, the review bar, a spend limit, no overrides. Only the developer's token records one; `--as` names the harness/model recording it for the developer, kept beside them. Every review brief of the project and `atelier guide --role orchestrate` carry the decisions that stand, marked as decisions a reviewer must not overrule.
Flags:
  --quote TEXT    the developer's own words the decision rests on; required, at most 2000 characters
  --project NAME  the project the decision is for; this checkout's or workspace's project unless given
  --as H/M        the harness/model recording the decision for the developer, kept beside them as its acting model
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier decide "Every change is reviewed by a model of another company" --quote "another company reviews everywhere" --project demo
decisions:
usage: atelier decisions [--all] [--project P]
       atelier decisions withdraw ID --note "why"
Lists the project's standing decisions, oldest first, each with its id, date, text and the developer's words. `--all` adds the withdrawn ones with their notes.
The developer withdraws a standing decision with a note saying why. It stops appearing in the briefs, the guide and the plain list; `--all` still shows it, withdrawn.
Flags:
  --all           adds the withdrawn decisions, each with its note
  --note TEXT     with withdraw, why; required, kept with the decision
  --project NAME  the project; this checkout's or workspace's project unless given
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier decisions --project demo
defect:
usage: atelier defect ID --note TEXT [--found-in ID] [--contradicts SEQ#N]
The developer traces a defect to the revision the task was accepted at. Nothing about the task changes; the reliability record counts the defect against the model that built that revision and against each model that approved it. `--found-in` names the task the defect was found or fixed in. `--contradicts` names a refuted or fixed verdict on one of this task's findings, by its event number and the finding's position, that the defect shows was wrong; it is refused for another task's or project's verdict, a confirmed one, or a review at a revision this task was not submitted at before its acceptance. The Models page counts it against the model that recorded the verdict, once however many defects name it; a defect that names no verdict counts against none.
Flags:
  --note TEXT          what is wrong; required
  --found-in ID        the task the defect was found or fixed in
  --contradicts SEQ#N  the verdict event (its number, as atelier finding and atelier receipt print it) and the finding it judged, which the defect shows was wrong; also tN@SEQ#N or PROJECT/tN@SEQ#N, naming this task and project
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier defect t3 --note "It drops the last row" --found-in t9 --contradicts 42#1 --project demo
diff:
usage: atelier diff ID
For a reviewer: prints the task's commits and diff against the baseline, from a clean read-only clone.
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier diff t3 --project demo
dispatch:
usage: atelier dispatch ID [--to home|cloud|any] [--agent A] [--model M] [--note T | --note-file PATH] [--job merge-main [--head H]] [--overlap-ok] [--release]
Queues an open task for a kind of runner, and optionally an agent and model, instead of waiting for an agent to choose it; a submitted or accepted task is released and queued in the same step, keeping its workspace, commits, reviews and acceptance history. An accepted task must be submitted and accepted again; a merge holding its landing lease must finish or be cancelled first. While the task's scope overlaps, within one of the project's core files (`init --core`), the scope of a claimed item or of the item a live landing lease names, the queue holds it and offers it to no runner until each claimed blocker submits or is released and the landing ends; `atelier status` and `atelier queue` name every item it waits on, and `--overlap-ok` lets this dispatch through at once. `--job merge-main` sends a task whose landing conflicted with main back to its builder: the runner fetches and merges the baseline's current main head at claim time into its workspace (`--head` records dispatch context, not the merge target) and leaves the conflicts for the builder to resolve and commit; then `atelier land ID` again. A task a builder holds live (claimed) is refused, naming the holder and when they claimed it, unless `--release` is given; `--release` ends that claim, says whose, and tells the holder at its next push or finish that the task was taken back. Developer only.
Flags:
  --to home|cloud|any  the kind of runner; any unless given
  --agent A            the agent the runner must run; --agent "" clears this restriction. Unless given, the server suggests a builder, except when --overlap-ok updates an existing dispatch
  --model M            the model the runner must use; --model "" clears this restriction independently of agent
  --note TEXT          a note the agent reads with the task, up to 2000 characters (UTF-16 code units); a longer note is refused, never cut
  --note-file PATH     the note is the text of the UTF-8 file at PATH, read relative to the current directory with its line breaks kept; not with --note; an unreadable or non-UTF-8 file is refused before anything is sent, and an empty file is an empty note
  --job merge-main     sends the task to its builder to merge main into its workspace and resolve the conflicts of a landing that stopped on them
  --head H             with --job merge-main, the full hash recorded as dispatch context; defaults to main's head as the baseline holds it at dispatch. It does not pin the merge target: the runner fetches and merges the baseline's current main head at claim time
  --release            takes a task a builder holds live (claimed): releases that claim, then queues the task as usual; without it the dispatch is refused and nothing changes
  --overlap-ok         records a core-file hold override and names the hold released, if any; preserves omitted fields of an existing dispatch without suggesting a builder. Does not bypass refuseOverlap; kept with this dispatch only
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier dispatch t3 --to home --agent codex --note "Keep it small" --project demo
done:
usage: atelier done "summary" [--json]
Pushes, runs the required checks and submits, in that order, and stops at the first step that fails, naming it. Its last line states the one outcome: `Outcome: submitted, ready for the developer`, `Outcome: checked but blocked by`, naming each blocker, or `Outcome: failed checks`, naming each failed check and any file a failed check left changed in the workspace. Above it are the head, the checks, the unresolved gates, whether it was submitted, acceptance, merge and deploy, and the developer's next action. `--json` prints the same as one object, its `outcome` field the outcome's name. Exit codes: 0 submitted and ready for the developer; 2 failed checks, nothing submitted; 3 checked but blocked, submitted with a gate still open; 1 a usage or other error; 4 a server or Artifacts step failed, with no outcome printed.
A local check runs on this machine with your file access: it can read your files and your Keychain and reach the network. It is given only PATH, HOME and the few other environment variables toolchains need, and Atelier's tokens are redacted from its output before it is uploaded. Atelier has no sandbox for checks: do not run code you do not trust.
Flags:
  --json  prints the outcome as one object; the progress goes to stderr
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier done "The parser takes the new form"
edit:
usage: atelier edit ID [--title TEXT] [--brief TEXT] [--scope GLOB]... [--accept TEXT]... [--non-goal TEXT]... [--stop-when TEXT]... [--next-gate TEXT] [--context TEXT]
The developer changes a task's title, brief, scope, acceptance criteria, non-goals, stop conditions next gate or context for the reviewers (the decisions a reviewer must not overrule, which every review brief carries). A flag given replaces that field, one left out keeps it, and an empty value clears it; the title cannot be cleared. A new scope is recorded in the task's history and counts at once for a project that refuses overlapping claims, which refuses a claim whose scope overlaps a claimed, submitted or accepted task's alike (a cancelled merge leaves a task accepted); an unscoped task overlaps every one. Changing the acceptance criteria (their text, order or entries) withdraws every review and open or claimed review request of the old ones, an acceptance (the task goes back to claimed) and an override of the review, and says so: a fresh review of the new criteria is needed. The same list again changes nothing. The criteria of an integrated part, or of a task being landed, cannot change.
Flags:
  --title TEXT      replaces the task's short title, at most 80 characters
  --brief TEXT      replaces the task's brief; --brief "" clears it
  --scope GLOB      replaces the task's scope; once per glob, or --scope "" alone to clear it (an unscoped task overlaps every other)
  --accept TEXT     replaces the task's acceptance criteria; once per criterion, or --accept "" alone to clear them
  --non-goal TEXT   replaces the task's non-goals; once per entry, or --non-goal "" alone to clear them
  --stop-when TEXT  replaces what tells the holder to stop and ask; once per entry, or --stop-when "" alone to clear it
  --next-gate TEXT  replaces the gate the task goes to next; --next-gate "" clears it
  --context TEXT    replaces the context every reviewer's brief carries, at most 2000 characters; --context "" clears it
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier edit t3 --stop-when "The schema needs to change" --project demo
fast:
usage: atelier fast take ID --as H/M [--runner home:NAME] [--dispatch AT] [--json]
       atelier fast ready ID --as H/M [--commit SHA]
       atelier fast status [--json] [--project P]
       atelier fast close [--project P]
In fast mode, takes a dispatched build without a fork: records the holder as a claim does, with no fork and no write token, and makes a clean clone of main for it on this machine. A clone that holds a commit an earlier run never reported is reported without a rebuild when it was made for the same dispatch; any other existing clone is moved aside to a .parked- folder beside it, never removed. A runner calls it in place of claim while the project is in fast mode.
In the clone fast take made, reports its head (or SHA) as ready to merge, with the main it was built on and the builder its Agent line names. Nothing is pushed; the developer merges it and records the merge with `record-merge`.
Prints the mode, every task landed in fast mode with its receipt and post-merge review state, and every build a runner made in fast mode and reported ready, one tN=SHA line each.

Run by the developer in the project checkout: creates the baseline repository in Artifacts, pushes the current branch to it, and records that branch as the project's branch, the required checks, the protected paths and an optional title. land:
usage: atelier land ID [--reviewer H/M] [--no-review] [--triage H/M | --no-triage REASON] [--override-triage REASON] [--wait] [--dry-run] [--release-lease] [--moved-ok] [--workflow [--checks local]]

The developer lands one task whole; a plan is refused before the lease, since it lands with `atelier merge ID --head H` at the integration head `plan show` prints and takes main through `plan refresh`. Review before the runway (t550): the merge of main, the checks and the review run without the project's landing lease, beside any other task's landing, and the lease is taken for the merge alone. It merges main into the task's workspace, stopping on conflicts and leaving them for the developer, naming the files. It regenerates the project's fixtures when the policy declares how (`init --regenerate`), pushes, runs the required checks and submits. With a triage model (`--triage H/M`, else the project's `triage` setting; neither runs none) it has that model, after the push and before the checks (whose passing evidence asks again for a review request the push withdrew from a task already submitted), read the pushed head's diff against its merge base with main and the task's acceptance criteria, and submits only when every criterion is met: a criterion not met or unsure, no criteria, an unreadable reply, a timeout or an unavailable model stops the landing before the review request, showing the findings and the commands to run again, the lease never taken and the task left with its holder. The developer may skip the triage with `--no-triage REASON` or go past a stop with `--override-triage REASON`; either is recorded with the head and the criteria binding first, and a record the server refuses stops the landing. Triage is recorded as land.triage events, never as a review, so the gate and the review rules after it are unchanged. An approval already recorded at the pushed head that the gate counts, the one `atelier show` recommends accept on (by the reviewer `--reviewer` names, where it names one), settles the review with no request and no wait. Otherwise it requests the independent review the gate needs through the review-request routes and waits for the verdict (up to 60 minutes, or ATELIER_LAND_REVIEW_TIMEOUT milliseconds), saying what the runners are busy with while the request is unclaimed, and, when no live runner offers the reviewer for the review job, that the request can never be claimed until one does, with the review by hand and the `--reviewer` that asks a model a runner offers. A named `--reviewer` is always asked, even where the gate needs no review, unless that reviewer's approval is already recorded so. A conflict, a failed check, a stopped triage or a rejection ends the landing with the lease never taken. Once the gate holds the pushed head with its checks passing and an approval it counts, the landing takes the project's landing lease, so two merges never race main, and confirms main is still the commit the head was merged with, checked and reviewed against; if another landing merged meanwhile it releases the lease without accepting, merges main again, checks it and asks for the review again (where the server's rules carry the approval over a clean merge of main, none is needed; otherwise a new review is waited for), and stops after five such rounds. Then it accepts and merges. Each step, its duration and the commits that came from main are recorded as land.* events, for the integration record, with the time spent before the lease and in its queue on the lease step and the time it was held on the release step (on a server that publishes land.review-first.v1; otherwise they are printed). It refuses to start when the server's route level is lower than this CLI's, saying to deploy. When another task's landing holds the lease as the checked and approved head reaches it, the landing queues behind it, with or without `--wait`: the server keeps the landings waiting for the lease in the order they queued and hands it to the first of them when it frees, so one landing cannot take it ahead of another that waited longer, however their polls land. While it waits the landing asks the server again on every poll, says whose landing it waits behind and which landings are queued ahead, and takes the lease when its turn comes (three hours at most, or ATELIER_LAND_WAIT_TIMEOUT milliseconds), so several landings started at once run in turn; a landing that stops asking drops out of the queue once 15 minutes pass without an ask. The lease is renewed while the landing runs, released on SIGINT or SIGTERM, and treated as free by the server once 15 minutes pass without a renewal, which the next landing reports when it takes the lease over. `--reviewer` names the reviewer; `--no-review` leaves the task submitted; `--wait` (the default since t550) queues for the lease, in the order the landings queued; `--dry-run` prints the steps and the refusals without changing anything; `--release-lease` frees the project's lease, saying which task held it since when. `--workflow` lands through a Cloudflare Workflow instead: the submission and the review wait run on the server as durable steps without the lease, then the lease, the check that main has not moved and the acceptance, each retried through transient failures (an Artifacts 503, a lost connection) and needing no token, while this command shows the Workflow's stage and does the steps that need Git with a working tree when the Workflow asks: merging main and pushing (holding no lease; again when main moved before the lease), and `atelier merge` once it holds the lease and has accepted. It needs a server that publishes land.review-first.v1. The required checks run on this machine in a clean clone of the pushed head, after any triage and before the head is reported, as the plain landing does, and the Workflow goes on only once the server has recorded every one passing, observed, at that head (failing ends the landing; no result within 30 minutes does too). A conflict pauses the Workflow, holding no lease, with the files named; resolve, commit and push them with `atelier push`, then run the same command again to resume. If the command stops (a closed laptop), the Workflow keeps its place: run it again to attach. `--dry-run` and `--workflow` together are refused.
Inspect or resolve a durable post-merge run. Status shows the policy, SHAs, ordered steps and attempts. Resume runs pending work; retry resumes a failed step; skip records a developer waiver and continues. Retry, skip and reconcile require a reason. Running or uncertain attempts require the developer to stop the executor and reconcile its external effect before retry or skip. Completed steps never replay and unresolved work blocks later merges.
Flags:
  --reason TEXT                     the developer’s explanation for retry, skip or reconciliation, recorded in history
  --resolution no-effect|completed  with reconcile, record the observed external effect after stopping the executor; a deployment still requires independent version verification or a waiver
  --post-merge ACTION               status shows the durable run and attempts; resume executes pending work; retry resumes a failed step; skip --reason records a waiver; reconcile --reason --resolution no-effect|completed settles uncertain effects after stopping the executor
  --reviewer H/M                    names the reviewer the request goes to, and the review is asked for even where the gate needs none; otherwise, when the gate needs a review, the server suggests a model of another company than every contributor (under single-family mode, a different model of the project's company) from the pool and the models' records, and the landing prints which and why
  --no-review                       skips waiting: the task is left submitted for the developer to settle the review by hand
  --triage H/M                      names the model that triages the merged diff against the task's acceptance criteria before the review is asked for, in place of the project's triage setting; same-company models may triage, and the pool's access and cost rules apply
  --no-triage REASON                skips the triage the project sets; the developer's reason is recorded with the head and the criteria binding before the landing goes on
  --override-triage REASON          goes on past a triage that stops; the developer's reason is recorded with the head and the criteria binding first. Neither this nor --no-triage stands in for the independent review
  --wait                            queues for the landing lease while another task's landing holds it, saying whose landing it waits behind and which landings are queued ahead; the server hands the lease to the waiting landings in the order they queued, so it merges when its turn comes (three hours at most). usage: atelier plan "goal" [--scope GLOB]... [--planner H/M]
       atelier plan show ID [--json]
       atelier plan approve ID --hash HASH [--allow-paid]
       atelier plan revise ID --note TEXT
       atelier plan reroute ID --to H/M
       atelier plan retry ID
       atelier plan refresh ID [--resolve [--to H/M]]
       atelier plan stop ID [--note TEXT]
       atelier plan post ID FILE
The developer states a goal. Atelier creates the plan task and queues it as a plan job for the planner named, or else for the first model in the pool for research work that is not refused, not paid per token and may plan. A project has one active plan at a time. A runner that offers plan jobs takes it: the planner claims the plan task, reads its brief from the job-brief route and posts the plan document the harness wrote; by hand, a planner claims with `--runner` and runs `plan post`.
Prints a plan: its phase, the newest proposal with its hash, or once approved each part with its state, dependencies, scope, routing and attempts, every claimed or landing item outside the plan a queued part waits on while the project's core files hold it and when each stops holding, any live review request naming the reviewer asked and whether a runner claimed it, and saying, when no live runner offers that reviewer for the review job, that the request can never be claimed until one does, with the reroute that names another, then the part dispatches used, why it is blocked, the main head the branch last took against main's head now with any refresh in flight or failed, and the command for each decision waiting on the developer. Before approval it shows the routing an approval would fix now, its reviewers judged against the live runner offers the same way. It accepts a part's id too.
Approves the split, once, by the hash of its newest proposal; an older hash is refused. The routing of each part is fixed then, with the limits: 2 parts live at once, 3 attempts a part, 4 dispatches a part, 24 hours. A part that no model can build, or that no independent model can review under the family policy (by default another family than every contributor; in single-family mode a different model of the selected company from every contributor), refuses the approval; a reviewer counts only when a live runner offers it for the review job, and when no runner is live the pool stands, with the routing saying so. `--allow-paid` lets models paid per token build and review.
Before approval, sends the plan back to its planner with a note; its next proposal replaces the one before.
Names who builds an open part from now on, its attempts counted afresh; for a submitted part, or one blocked for want of an eligible reviewer, names its reviewer, in the pool or not, which must be of another family than every contributor by default, or in single-family mode a different model of the selected company from every contributor; before approval, names another planner for the plan.
Counts an open part's attempts afresh, so its builder is asked again; before approval, asks the planner again.
Queues the plan's refresh job for the integrator, which merges main's head into the plan's branch, so later parts fork from it; parts wait for it before they are dispatched. The tick does this itself before it dispatches a part when main has moved, once per main head; this runs it again, as after a failed refresh. On a plan submitted or accepted, it first withdraws the submission and any acceptance and puts the plan back to building, and says so; the integrator submits it again once every part is integrated on a branch that holds main. It is refused before approval, once the plan is closed, while the plan's integrate or refresh job is queued or held, while a merge of the plan holds its landing lease, and when the branch already holds main's head. A refresh that conflicts adds a merge-main part to the plan, which a model builds: the runner merges main into the part's workspace and leaves the conflicts for it to resolve, and its integration puts main on the branch; no other part is dispatched until it is integrated. `--resolve` adds that part for main's head now without trying a refresh first, built by `--to` when named; it is refused while a refresh is queued, when the part for that head exists, while another merge-main part is not integrated, and when the branch already holds main's head.
Closes the plan and every part not yet merged, revoking their write tokens. The history and evidence stay.
The holder of the plan task's claim, its planner, posts the plan document in FILE. An invalid one is refused with every error, and the planner gets one more attempt before the plan blocks.

  --scope GLOB   with a goal, a path pattern the plan is to touch; once per pattern
  --planner H/M  with a goal, the model that plans the work
  --json         with show, prints the plan as JSON
  --hash HASH    with approve, the full hash of the newest proposal
  --allow-paid   with approve, lets models paid per token build parts
  --note TEXT    with revise or stop, why; kept with the event
  --to H/M       with reroute, the model that builds from now on, reviews a submitted part, or plans before approval; with refresh --resolve, the model that builds the merge-main part
  --resolve      with refresh, adds a part that merges main's head into the branch and resolves its conflicts, instead of queuing a refresh
