  --expected-head SHA                       the task's head the lease found
  --outcome mechanical|returned|superseded  what ended a task's refresh
  --report FILE                             the conflict report, as JSON, for a returned or mechanical conflict
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier refresh-failed t3 --main-head 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567 --reason "Conflict in docs/a.md" --kind conflict --project demo
refresh-lease:
usage: atelier refresh-lease ID [--job refresh|resolve] [--runner NAME]
       atelier refresh-lease ID (--renew LEASE | --release LEASE [--reason TEXT] [--provider-limit] | --status LEASE)
Takes the lease a task's refresh runs under (t462): the integrator's for merging main into the task's head, a resolver's for resolving the mechanical conflicts that merge left. Refused while the task is busy or blocked, with why. Prints the lease, the task's head it found, the main head to merge, and tokens to fetch main and push to the task's fork; the write token is revoked when the lease settles.
The leaseholder renews its lease through a long run (a resolver's harness, the required checks), or gives it back with no outcome: a provider's usage limit stopped its harness, or the job failed before it could report anything else. A released lease leaves the refresh as it was before it, queued, or waiting for the same resolver, and its write token is revoked. A lease that announced a push (refresh-pushing) is not given back: the push is never taken back off the fork, and once the lease lapses its announcer or the integrator reconciles it, recording the pushed head or finding the fork elsewhere. The developer alone may release such a lapsed push with `--release LEASE --reason TEXT`, ending the landing fence and queuing the refresh again; what the fork then holds is the developer's to check. --status prints the task's head as recorded now and whether the lease is still live and running checks, which a leaseholder whose report went unanswered reads to say where its push stands.
Flags:
  --job refresh|resolve  refresh (the integrator's, the default) or resolve (the resolver's)
  --runner NAME          the runner that runs the job, recorded with the lease
  --renew LEASE          renew the lease its holder runs under
  --release LEASE        give the lease back with no outcome; the developer, with --reason, releases a lapsed lease's unreconciled push
  --status LEASE         read the task's recorded head and whether the lease is live
  --reason TEXT          why the lease is given back, kept in the task's log
  --provider-limit       the lease is given back because a provider's usage limit stopped the harness
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier refresh-lease t3 --project demo --as atelier/integrator
refresh-pushing:
usage: atelier refresh-pushing ID --lease ID --main-head SHA --expected-head SHA --head SHA
A task refresh's leaseholder says it pushes the refreshed merge next (t462). Refused when the task moved from the head the lease found, or is busy or landing; taken, no landing of the task begins until the push is reconciled: recorded by the leaseholder, or, once its lease lapses, by the integrator's next refresh job, or released by the developer with `refresh-lease ID --release LEASE --reason TEXT`.
Flags:
  --lease ID           the lease refresh-lease gave
  --main-head SHA      the main head the refresh merged
  --expected-head SHA  the task's head the lease found
  --head SHA           the refreshed merge about to be pushed
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier refresh-pushing t3 --lease 0f3c... --main-head 0123... --expected-head 4567... --head 89ab... --project demo
refreshed:
usage: atelier refreshed ID --lease ID --main-head SHA --expected-head SHA [--head SHA] [--diff-before ID --diff-after ID] [--transformations LIST]
       atelier refreshed ID --main-head SHA [--merge-commit SHA]
A task refresh's leaseholder reports the merge it pushed (t462): the server checks it is the fork's head, with the head the lease found and main's head as its parents, and that its Agent line names who made it: the integrator for a clean merge, or the resolver for a resolved one, who joins the task's contributors. The task's head becomes the merge; an accepted task goes back to submitted, and the new head needs its own review. Without `--head` the task's head already held main. A repeated report answers the recorded outcome.
The integrator reports a refresh: main's head, the one the refresh job names, merged into the plan's branch. The server checks the merge commit against the branch before recording it, and it becomes the commit later parts fork from and later integrations build on. Without `--merge-commit` the branch already held main's head, which the server checks.
Flags:
  --main-head SHA         the full hash of the main head the refresh merged; required
  --merge-commit SHA      the full hash of the merge commit on the plan's branch; left out when the branch already held main's head
  --lease ID              a task refresh's lease, which refresh-lease gave
  --expected-head SHA     the task's head the lease found
  --head SHA              the refreshed merge pushed to the task's fork; left out when the task already held main
  --diff-before ID        the patch id of the task's own diff before the refresh
  --diff-after ID         the patch id of the task's own diff against main after it
  --transformations LIST  the mechanical transformations a resolver's merge applied, comma-separated
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier refreshed t3 --main-head 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567 --merge-commit 89abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef --project demo
refreshes:
usage: atelier refreshes [--enqueue] [--json]
Lists the tasks queued to take main as it moves (t462): every unfinished task outside a plan with a branch of its own (open after a release, submitted or accepted), with the main head it should take, what its refresh is doing, and, for a busy or blocked task, why its refresh waits: a builder holds it, it is blocked, a runner is about to rebuild it, a review of its head is under way, or it is landing. A task with no commits of its own is not listed, since a claim starts it from main as main is then. A recorded merge queues the refreshes; `--enqueue` reads main's head now and queues it, for main moved outside Atelier. The integrator's runner (atelier runner --integrate) merges each in a workspace of its own; a mechanical conflict goes to a resolver (atelier init --resolver), any other back to the builder with the merge base, both heads, the paths and the hunks.
Flags:
  --enqueue  reads main's head now and queues it for every task that should take it
  --json     prints the queue as the server answers it
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier refreshes --project demo
release:
usage: atelier release ID [--note TEXT]
Gives the task up: it returns to open and the write token is revoked.
Flags:
  --note TEXT  why; kept with the release
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier release t3 --note "Blocked on the schema"
report:
usage: atelier report [ID] "what you verified and how" [--item ID] [--project P]
Records a Reported claim at the current head: what the agent verified and how. It goes on the task named, else on the workspace's task; in a workspace, another task's id needs `--item ID`. It is shown and never counted as a check.
Flags:
  --item ID    the task the claim goes on, when it is not the workspace's
  --project P  with an ID, records the claim there even from another task's workspace
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier report "Ran the app by hand; the parser takes the new form"
revert:
usage: atelier revert ID

Creates a new task that undoes a recorded merge with git revert -m1, under the normal checks and independent review. Both tasks keep a link in the ledger. Conflicts remain in the new workspace for resolution.

Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.

Example: atelier revert t7
review:
usage: atelier review ID --approve|--reject --criteria BINDING [--request N] [--note TEXT] [--head SHA] [--findings JSON]
Records a verdict on the task's current head, or its recorded merge commit when the task is merged, with `--note` giving the reason. `--head` names the revision the verdict is for; on a merged task it must explicitly name the recorded merge SHA given by the review claim, rather than the submitted head, and `--request` must name the post-merge review request the reviewer claimed. The server refuses a verdict for any other revision. `--criteria` names the binding of the acceptance criteria the verdict judged, as `atelier show` or the review claim gives it; the server refuses a verdict that names none, or criteria the task no longer has, and the reviewer must read them again. `--request` names the review request the reviewer claimed, which the verdict then answers alone; without it, the verdict answers the request this machine last claimed for the task as this reviewer (`atelier review-claim`), and says which. `--findings` attaches a reviewer's structured findings. The rules say whose approval counts.
Flags:
  --approve           records an approval
  --reject            records a rejection
  --note TEXT         the reason, shown with the verdict
  --head SHA          the revision the verdict is for; defaults to the task's current head before merge; on a merged task, required and must name the recorded merge SHA from the review claim, with --request naming the claimed post-merge review request; any other revision is refused
  --criteria BINDING  the binding of the acceptance criteria the verdict judged, as atelier show or the review claim gives it; required, and refused once the criteria change
  --request N         the review request the reviewer claimed, as the claim gives it; defaults to the one this machine last claimed for the task as this reviewer; required after merge; the verdict answers it alone, and is refused once it is withdrawn
  --findings JSON     a JSON list of the reviewer's findings, kept with the verdict
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier review t3 --approve --criteria BINDING --note "The tests cover the new form" --as claude-code/opus-5.5
review-claim:
usage: atelier review-claim ID --as H/M [--runner home:NAME]
       atelier review-claim ID --renew --as H/M [--request N]
A reviewer's runner claims the task's open review request and gets the part, its brief's inputs, the binding of the acceptance criteria the brief carries and the request's number, which the verdict names, and a read token for its fork. The claim prints as one JSON line, then, for a reviewer serving it by hand, the request, head and criteria binding, the exact `atelier review` command that records the verdict, and that the lease lasts 5 minutes; this machine remembers the request for `atelier review` and `--renew`.
Renews the 5-minute lease on a review request claimed by hand, as a runner renews its own, for the reviewer that claimed it, named with `--as` as the claim named it; without `--request`, the request this machine last claimed for the task. The server skips a renewal within 30 seconds of the last, so renew every 2 minutes.
Flags:
  --runner home:NAME  names the runner that claims the review request
  --renew             renews the lease on the claimed request rather than claiming one
  --request N         with --renew, the request to renew, as the claim gave it; defaults to the one this machine last claimed for the task
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier review-claim t3 --runner home:studio --project demo
review-release:
usage: atelier review-release ID [--request N] [--note T]
Release the review claim for the actor named by --as, so another reviewer may take it. Agents and runners must send --request with the number returned by review-claim; stale numbers cannot release a successor's claim. Only the developer's credentials may omit --request to recover the actor's current claim.
Flags:
  --request N  the current claim's request number; required for agents and runners
  --note TEXT  why the review request is let go; kept with the event
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier review-release t3 --request 7 --note "The harness wrote no verdict" --project demo
review-request:
usage: atelier review-request ID --reviewer H/M [--hand]
The developer queues a review for a runner. A merged task is reviewed at its recorded merge commit against the merge's original parent (or fork point for a fast-forward), with the task's criteria. Verdicts and findings stay on the task and count on Models; blocking findings file a linked defect task. The merged task stays merged, including when it landed on an override.
Flags:
  --reviewer H/M  the independent reviewer whose runner audits the recorded merge
  --hand          open the request although no live runner offers the review job, for a review the developer serves by hand with review-claim --runner home:hand
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier review-request t3 --reviewer codex/gpt-6-astra --project demo
review-unparsable:
usage: atelier review-unparsable ID --head SHA --note TEXT --reply-file PATH
Keeps a reviewer's reply that no verdict could be read from on the task, its last 100 KB with the reviewer and the head, and lets the review request go as review-release does. The runner calls it when the reply states no verdict; the reliability record counts the reply against the reviewer, and atelier show ID --reviews prints it.
Flags:
  --head SHA         the full revision the review read; required
  --note TEXT        why no verdict could be read, as the parser said it; kept with the reply
  --reply-file PATH  the file the harness wrote the reply to; its last 100 KB is kept; required
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier review-unparsable t3 --head 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567 --note "No VERDICT line" --reply-file verdict.txt --project demo
review-withdraw:
usage: atelier review-withdraw ID --reason TEXT [--request N]
The developer withdraws an open review request no runner has claimed, with the reason, kept on the task. The gate then asks no one until the developer asks again, of any reviewer, at the same head (atelier land ID --reviewer H/M); a plan's part is asked of another reviewer its routing allows, never the withdrawn one at that head, or waits for the developer. A claimed request is being served and is refused: its verdict, or its claim lapsing, ends it. atelier land --reviewer naming another reviewer withdraws an unclaimed request in the same way, and says so.
Flags:
  --reason TEXT  why the request is withdrawn; required, kept with the event
  --request N    the request to withdraw, by number; defaults to the newest request at the task's head
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier review-withdraw t3 --reason "No runner serves codex/gpt-6-astra" --project demo
run-report:
usage: atelier run-report --actor H/M --role build|review --outcome KIND [--project P] [--item ID] [--detail TEXT]
The developer records a run that ended without a result the ledger saw, for a run outside the runner: an early stop, a permission stop, a duplicate design or an incomplete merge, beside stalled, timed-out and refused, which the runner reports itself. The reliability record counts it against the actor, and a review run counts as a review that never reached a verdict.
Flags:
  --actor H/M          the harness/model the run ran; required
  --role build|review  build or review; build unless given
  --outcome KIND       stalled, timed-out, refused, early_stop, permission_stop, duplicate_design or incomplete_merge; required
  --project P          the project the run was in
  --item ID            the task the run was on
  --detail TEXT        what happened
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier run-report --actor opencode/glm-5.3 --role build --outcome early_stop --project atelier --item t114 --detail "stopped after a refused read"
runner:
usage: atelier runner --name home:NAME [--once] [--config PATH] [--integrate] [--replace]
       atelier runner --discover [--name home:NAME] [--probe] [--dry-run] [--config PATH]
       atelier runner --usage [--name home:NAME] [--dry-run] [--config PATH]
The home runner: polls the queue every 30 seconds, claims one eligible task and runs its configured harness in the claimed workspace. Each opencode run gets a data folder of its own beside the workspace, removed when the run ends, because opencode runs that share one deadlock on its database. When the harness commits, the runner runs `finish`. `--integrate` runs no harness: it offers only the integrate and refresh jobs and merges each part onto its plan's branch as atelier/integrator. `--once` handles at most one task. It refuses to start when a runner of the same name already runs on this Mac, naming its pid; `--replace` stops that process first.
Reports which model each home harness actually served, from the records the harness keeps, and sends the result to the server as each model's status. `--probe` also sends one short prompt to each model that can be probed; `--dry-run` reports nothing.
Reports how much of each tool's allowance this machine has used: Codex's 5-hour and weekly windows, the requests and tokens zcode, opencode and Claude Code recorded by served model over the last 5 hours, 24 hours and 7 days (with cost, for opencode), and the DeepSeek balance when the runner config names its Keychain entry. After the tools' own figures it prints what the server read of the AI Gateway: each model's calls, tokens, cost and durations, and the calls per task the runners' cf-aig-metadata tags name; then each model's speed over the last 14 days (median build, review and claim-to-merge times with n, and the share of runs that stalled). Each tool's summary goes to the server under the runner's name, for the Usage page and its alerts; `--dry-run` reports nothing. It runs once, not as part of the runner loop. Claude Code's tokens by model per day are read from its session logs (counts only). Claude's plan percent, Antigravity and Gemini's spend are listed under Not reported with the reason and the best figure there is.
Flags:
  --name home:NAME  this runner's name; home: and this machine's host name unless given
  --once            handles at most one task, then exits
  --config PATH     the runner config file; runner.json in the config folder unless given
  --integrate       runs no harness; offers only the integrate and refresh jobs and merges each part onto its plan's branch
  --replace         stops a live runner of the same name on this Mac, then starts; without it the start is refused
  --discover        reports which model each home harness served, as each model's status
  --probe           with --discover, also sends one short prompt to each model that can be probed
  --dry-run         prints what would be reported and reports nothing
  --usage           reports each tool's windows, served models, costs and balances
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier runner --name home:studio --once
served:
usage: atelier served MODEL --recorded H/M --from TIME --to TIME [--item ID]... [--note T] [--apply]
The developer records which model served events recorded under another, as when zcode served deepseek-flash while its events named glm-5.3. Each event recorded as `--recorded` from `--from` up to `--to`, on the tasks `--item` names or on every task, gets an annotation of its own, and the track record, the reliability record and the graph count it under the served model; the event itself never changes. Without `--apply` it lists the matches and records nothing. `--note` says how the developer knows.
Flags:
  --recorded H/M  the actor the events were recorded under
  --from TIME     the start of the span, as a date and time
  --to TIME       the end of the span, up to which events are counted
  --item ID       limits it to one task, once per task; every task unless given
  --note TEXT     how the developer knows which model served them
  --apply         records the annotations; without it, only lists the matches
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier served deepseek-flash --recorded zcode/glm-5.3 --from 2026-10-01T00:00 --to 2026-10-03T00:00 --apply
ship:
usage: atelier ship [--dry-run] [--push]
Run by the developer in the registered checkout, clean and at the baseline's head: composes the ship order from the project's ControlPlane ship policy and adapter, or from `docs/atelier/ship.json`, and refuses before running anything when a protected step has no approval at that revision, naming the command that approves it. It then runs the steps in order and stops at the first that fails, recording each step's command, exit status, duration and redacted output tail on the ledger. It pushes only with `--push`, which needs no approval since ship is developer-only and runs at one exact revision, and never forces a push; a remote the project declares a public mirror (`init --public-mirror`) takes only commits under the project's no-reply address. `--dry-run` prints the steps and which approvals are present or missing, and runs nothing.
Flags:
  --dry-run  composes the ship order and checks its approvals, running nothing
  --push     also pushes the registered branch to the project's own remotes; the developer's own act at this revision, needing no separate approval
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier ship --dry-run --project demo
show:
usage: atelier show ID [--reviews] [--json]
Prints a task's decision brief: what is decided, the brief the developer filed it with (without claiming the task, as `start` does), the recorded evidence, a recommendation and the task's address. When a required check fails at the current head as the gate reads it (the latest counting run of each check at that head, and a failing run on the merge with main that blocks), it also prints each failed check by command, head and evidence id (and container run id), the failing tests its reporter named (node:test, TAP, vitest, jest, pytest, go test, cargo test, XCTest and swift-testing are read; any other output, or a typecheck, says the names are unavailable, and a log kept as a tail may have lost the lines naming them, which is said, unless the run kept the lines naming its failure from the whole output, which are then read and printed first), and the last 20 lines, at most 2,000 characters, of its log, the whole log read from where it is stored or the inline tail labelled as such. `--reviews` also prints each review at each head with its whole note and findings, then the reviews of the acceptance criteria themselves with the developer's resolutions; `--json` prints the brief, carrying the filed brief as `brief`, the reviews, the criteria reviews and the failed checks, for scripts.
Flags:
  --reviews  prints each review at each head, with its whole note and every finding; a tier review is labelled as one, and a gate review by a tier model as the gate review, top tier; then the reviews of the acceptance criteria themselves, with each revision's author, their findings and the developer's resolutions
  --json     prints the brief as JSON, with every review and its findings, and the record of the criteria reviews
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier show t3 --project demo
slots:
usage: atelier slots set N
       atelier slots status [--json]
Atomically sets this machine's test-slot capacity to a positive safe integer. Running work drains normally; waiting work keeps its priority and FIFO order. Update every runner before changing capacity.
Shows configured capacity, active usage, draining excess and waiting work. Runs locally without server credentials.
Flags:
  --json  prints status as JSON
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier slots set 3
start:
usage: atelier start ID [--as H/M] [--runner home:NAME]
Claims the task, prepares its workspace as `claim` does, and prints its title, brief, acceptance criteria, scope and any dispatch note. `--runner` names the runner when a runner claims a dispatched task.
Flags:
  --runner home:NAME  names the runner, when a runner claims a dispatched task
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier start t3 --project demo --as claude-code/opus-5.5
status:
usage: atelier status [--project P] [--brief] [--json]
Prints the developer's queue for every project: what waits for the developer, which pairs of live tasks name overlapping scopes (each pair once, nothing waiting on them), what is in progress and what waits for a runner, with every claimed or landing item each dispatch the project's core files holds waits on and when each stops holding, each open review request among it with its reviewer named, and, for any queued job no live runner offers, that it can never be claimed until a runner that offers it is started, which is a mismatch between the dispatch and the runners rather than a wait. The developer's branches of every project follow, each with its last commit and the Mac it was pushed from. It warns first, under Usage warnings, of each vendor window at 80 percent used or heading past its limit before it resets, naming the vendor, window and reset time, and of a usage report not heard from in 3 hours as unknown; then, under Token expiries, from 14 days before each named token's recorded expiry day (`atelier ops token-expiry NAME --on YYYY-MM-DD` records it), naming the token and the date. With `--project` it prints where one project stands instead, ending with whether this checkout is in step with the baseline, the developer's branches (`atelier branch`) with each one's last commit and the Mac it was pushed from, and, when any of the project's tasks has a workspace on this Mac, an On this Mac section: each live task's workspace with its uncommitted changes, commits not pushed to its fork, a merge in progress and a waiting COMMIT_MSG.txt, a count of the merged or abandoned tasks' workspaces left behind, and whether a landing is running here for the project. Both full text forms also list this machine’s live runners and task workspace processes by task, with process ids and ages, never full command lines. With `--project --json`, these appear under `processes`. `--brief` prints the report to give the developer after each landing, in under 20 lines: the recent merges, the commit the server is deployed at, live builds, reviews and the landing running, and 24-hour spend against the daily limit. `--json` prints machine-readable records, each task with its created, updated and last-push times, as Observatory reads them, the overlapping pairs under `overlaps` and the same local facts under `local`.
Flags:
  --brief      the report to give the developer after each landing, in under 20 lines: recent merges, the deployed commit, live builds, reviews and landings, and spend against the daily limit; the project is --project, else this checkout's
  --project P  where one project stands, as text, instead of the developer's queue for every project; ends with an On this Mac section when any of its tasks has a workspace here
  --json       prints machine-readable records, each item with its created, updated and last-push times and each project's overlapping task pairs under `overlaps`; with --project, also the local facts of this Mac's workspaces and any landing
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier status --project demo
stuck:
usage: atelier stuck [--project P] [--json] [--no-push-hours N] [--unanswered-hours N] [--lease-wait-minutes N] [--conflict-wait-minutes N] [--core-hold-minutes N] [--runner-poll-minutes N] [--review-answer-hours N]
One read-only developer report of stuck tasks, lease waits, conflict pauses, confirmed orphan leases, runner give-ups, idle polls, claims orphaned by a runner that stopped polling, claimed reviews and stale core holds; prints evidence and recovery commands without running them, and separately lists failed observed check commands in the preceding rolling day.
Flags:
  --project P                developer-only read-only report for this project (defaults to the checkout's project); failed reads are unavailable, never empty evidence
  --json                     prints observation time, limits, evidence ages and links, recovery commands, unavailable sources and failed observed check commands in the preceding rolling day
  --no-push-hours N          positive limit for claims; default 6 hours
  --unanswered-hours N       positive limit for unanswered changes requests; default 24 hours
  --lease-wait-minutes N     positive limit for lease-stage Workflows; default 30 minutes
  --conflict-wait-minutes N  positive limit for Workflows paused at conflict; default 30 minutes; resolve, commit and push conflicts with atelier push, then rerun land ID --workflow
  --core-hold-minutes N      positive limit for core blockers since their current claim/handoff or later push; default 30 minutes; land the blocker (merge if already accepted) or dispatch the held task with --overlap-ok if harmless
  --runner-poll-minutes N    positive idle-poll limit; default 5 minutes, plus one minute of offer timestamp coarsening; a runner with an active job is not idle. A claim is orphaned by its runner past the fixed 5 minutes (plus the minute), whatever this says, since that is when it stops holding the core files; a runner mid-job renews its poll with a heartbeat
  --review-answer-hours N    positive limit for current claimed reviews; default 2 hours; a claim ages from when it began, not its last renewal; a re-claim after expiry starts a new claim
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier stuck --project demo
submit:
usage: atelier submit [--summary T]
Marks the task ready for the developer and prints what still blocks it, if anything. `--summary` stores a summary of the change with the submission.
Flags:
  --summary TEXT  a summary of the change, stored with the submission
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier submit --summary "The parser takes the new form"
sync:
usage: atelier sync
Refreshes the stored policy from the project's ControlPlane files. For a baseline built with `--history-since`, it also carries commits made in the checkout outside Atelier to the baseline. Refused before anything is sent, the policy included, while main does not hold the baseline's main (`pull` brings it in).
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier sync --project demo
token:
usage: atelier token issue --as H/M [--project P]... [--days N] [--label TEXT]
       atelier token ls
       atelier token revoke ID
The developer issues a token bound to one actor and shown once. It expires in 30 days unless `--days` (1 to 365) says otherwise, and covers the named projects or all of them.
Lists token records without the tokens or their hashes.
Revokes a token; later API requests with it are refused. Git credentials already issued keep their own lifetime.
Flags:
  --as H/M      the actor the token is bound to; every request with it must name that actor
  --project P   limits the token to the named projects, once per project; without it, every project
  --days N      how many days the token lasts, 1 to 365; 30 unless given
  --label TEXT  a label kept with the token's record, to tell tokens apart in token ls
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier token issue --as codex/gpt-6-astra --project demo --days 7
unblock:
usage: atelier unblock [ID]
The holder or the developer lifts the block, and the task returns to the state it was in; it also lifts the fence a blocking pre-review left on the task's landing, so atelier land can queue it again.
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier unblock t3 --project demo
undispatch:
usage: atelier undispatch ID
Takes the task out of the queue.
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier undispatch t3 --project demo
unwrap:
usage: atelier unwrap [--project P]
Reads where the project stands, the state of this checkout, where its branch stands against each of the checkout's remotes as last fetched or pushed, the newest session note, the state file (the first of `docs/STATE.md`, `STATE.md` and `PROJECT.md` that exists) and any dated handoffs. It fetches and writes nothing. The developer's session starts here.
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier unwrap --project demo
update:
usage: atelier update
Brings the workspace up to date: first with commits another holder pushed to the fork, then with whatever has merged to the baseline since the fork. Each step is previewed first, and a declaration problem the result would hold, such as a command name both sides declare, stops it with nothing moved. Where the step needs a generator declared in bin/merge-manifest.json, because both sides changed what it reads, it merges through the merge pipeline, which regenerates the outputs, and names `atelier push`; otherwise it rebases through the clone's merge drivers and names `atelier push --force`, whose lease refuses to overwrite anything pushed since the workspace last fetched.
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier update
wait:
usage: atelier wait ID [--for merged|submitted|reviewed|any-change] [--timeout SECONDS] [--interval SECONDS]
Blocks until the task reaches that state, or fails, and prints the outcome as one line; the default is `merged`. `merged` waits for the merge, `submitted` for the submission (a task already further on counts), `reviewed` for a review recorded at the task's current head and acceptance criteria (an approval is reached, a rejection fails), and `any-change` for the task's state, head, holder or review count to differ from the first read. A task that is abandoned or blocked fails every wait but `any-change`. It polls every 5 seconds and rides through a server that is briefly unreachable. Exit status: 0 reached, 1 failed, 3 gave up at `--timeout` (no limit by default), 4 the task could not be read. It replaces a hand-written `pgrep` or `lsof` loop, which matches its own command line and misses a death.
Flags:
  --for STATE         merged (the default), submitted, reviewed or any-change
  --timeout SECONDS   gives up after this long, exit status 3; with no limit by default
  --interval SECONDS  how often it reads the task; 5 by default
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier wait t3 --for reviewed --project demo
wrap:
usage: atelier wrap "summary" [--next TEXT] [--found TEXT]... [--push] [--no-check | --allow-failing] [--project P]
Closes the developer's session in the registered checkout: runs the registered checks and, when every one passes, commits everything with the summary as its subject, updates the baseline and records a session note on the ledger. A failing check refuses the commit, naming each failed check with how it ended, and leaves the checkout, the ledger and every remote as they were; `--allow-failing` commits anyway, and the note records which checks it let through. Check results are Reported, because they ran on the developer's machine. `--push` also pushes the checkout's own remotes; `--found` files a task for each defect found; `--no-check` skips the checks.
Flags:
  --next TEXT      what the next session should do; recorded in the note and the commit message
  --found TEXT     files a task with this title; once per defect found, at most 100
  --push           also pushes the registered branch to each of the checkout's own remotes
  --no-check       skips the registered checks; the note records that they were skipped
  --allow-failing  commits past a failing check; the note names each check let through
Every command also takes --project NAME and --as harness/model (or ATELIER_ACTOR); --help prints this.
Example: atelier wrap "Fixed the parser" --next "Add the tests"
